The '''2003–04 [[La Liga]]''' season was the 73rd since its establishment. It began on 30 August 2003, and concluded on 23 May 2004. [[Valencia CF|Valencia]] were crowned champions for the sixth time in club history.

As of 2026, this is most recent season in which the title went to a team other than [[FC Barcelona|Barcelona]], [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]], and [[Atlético Madrid|Atletico Madrid]].

==Teams==
Twenty teams competed in the league&nbsp;– the top seventeen teams from the previous season and the three teams promoted from the [[2002–03 Segunda División|Segunda División]]. The promoted teams were [[Real Murcia|Murcia]], [[Real Zaragoza|Zaragoza]] and [[Albacete Balompié|Albacete]], returning to the top flight after an absence of fourteen, one and seven years respectively. They replaced [[Recreativo de Huelva|Recreativo]], [[Deportivo Alavés|Alavés]], and [[Rayo Vallecano]] after spending time in the top flight for one, five, and four years respectively.
